body:
larrybob@io.com (Laurence Roberts) wrote:
> I agree with many of the arguments you make in your manifesto, but I do not
> agree with your methods.

So what are you doing to fix things?  Nothing?  What a surprise.

> Ted, they say you are a psychopath.  I'm inclined to agree, because of
> an especially damning piece of evidence, namely your letter to Dr. David
> Gelernter, the author of the book Mirror Worlds, and one of the victims
> of your bombs.  You sent a bomb to him because you did not agree with the
> ideas which he expressed in his book.

Dr. Gelernter was sent a bomb because he was part of the problem,
specifically an advocate of the technoindustrial system.  Bombings are
disruptive to computer nerds and help break down computer science study
programs.

> Ted, that is not reasonable behavior.  If you don't agree with someone's
> ideas, send them a letter, not a bomb.

A letter will change nothing and not enlighten an ignorant individual,
while a bomb changes things.

71. [...] One may become angry, but modern society cannot permit
fighting.  [...]

72. Modern society is in certain respects extremely permissive.  In
matters that are irrelvant to the functioning of the system we can
generally do what we please.  We can believe in any religion we like (as
long as it does not encourage behavior that is dangerous to the system).
We can go to bed with anyone we like (as long as we practice "safe
sex").  We can do anything we like as long as it is UNIMPORTANT.  But in
all IMPORTANT matters the system tends increasingly to regulate our
behavior.

> (The point of this letter isn't to analyze your philosophy, but I can't
> help pointing out an inconsistency.

Your point below displays willful ignorance.

> In your letter to Gelernter, you
> accuse him of elitism for saying that people with a college education
> will be able to cope in a computer-based society.

Correct.  A college degree should not be the basis for one's position in
society, as it is not a measure of intelligence.

> What about the
> statement in section 188 of your manifesto?  "On a second level, the
> ideology should be propagated in a simplified form that will enable
> the unthinking majority to see the conflict of technology vs. nature in
> unambiguous terms."  Sounds a hypocritical to me.

Not at all.  The majority of people in the world are unthinking,
incredibly stupid people.  That's why the world has so many problems.
Maybe 5% are worth anything at all.  Intelligence is rare.  But any herd
beast can be educated and collect degrees.

> How ironic that
> you, with a PhD in mathematics, start your letter to Gelernter
> "People with advanced degrees aren't as smart as they think they are.")

It is unfortunate that you are unable to accept the truth in that statement,
even when issued from someone who understood the falacy of "degrees =
intelligence."

> Your goals may be worthy, but your methods not only are unjustifiable,
> they stand no chance of working.  To make mass changes in society
> requires mass movements of people, not bombing campaigns, of whatever
> size.  Perhaps you were unable to relate to other people in order
> to become involved in a mass movement.

Thousands of environmentalists and social radicals have seen the light
and are moving forward to carry the torch of revolution as they have
been shown.  The mass changes in society are coming - not everything
happens overnight.

> Your life has been a waste.  You could have devoted the effort used to
> making bombs to writing and persuading people to your point of view.

The bombs and writing have persuaded thousands of people who were
impressed with his honesty and intelligence.

> Your manifesto was flawed, in need of editing and critique.  But because
> myou chose to shut yourself off from a community of like-minded individuals,
> even the potential of your manifesto was unrealized.

You obviously didn't understand something and fault the writer for your
inability.

> You attempted to topple the giant of the spectacle, but instead you
> have been incorporated into the spectacle.  Few people paid serious
> attention to your manifesto.  Your manifesto helped sell advertisements
> in the newspapers.

Few people can think in today's society, but those who can are taking
action to redeem society.

> Ted, I think you have potential to do good in order to begin to make
> up for the hurt that you have caused others.  Keep working on your
> writing, since that will probably be the area in which you will be
> able to interact with other people.

The technoindustrial pigs have not suffered enough.  Ted is not here to
"do good" to your system, he is here to crush it and let it die because
of its deceit and stupidity.  Why should he respect your system of lies
and error?

You really don't get a word he wrote do you?  It's like you're from
another planet.

-Ric
